clue.text: Changing form of punishment?

definitions.meaning: swapping one thing for another, as in changing trains
beating with a thin flexible stick, a once-common punishment

explanation.surface: A question about how punishment might change its form.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: altering or exchanging, and thrashing someone with a cane-like rod.

clue.text: Philosopher's treatment of topics not primarily philosophical

indicators.note: a treatment of something works it over, so the letters are reworked into a new order
not tells us a letter is to be left out of the word topics
primarily points to the opening letter of the word philosophical

explanation.surface: A thinker deals with subjects that are not mainly philosophical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not primarily philosophical' takes P out of TOPICS, leaving TOICS, which 'treatment of' rearranges; the 's after 'Philosopher' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of Zeno's school of thought in ancient Athens.

clue.text: In pub by church you get fish served in sauce

indicators.note: the fish is served inside the pub, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole is a flatfish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A diner orders fish in a sauce at a pub next to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like part of the meal but is the definition, in its British sense of cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang sauce means cheek or impudent talk, which is rudeness.

clue.text: Ancient Roman battle ground

parts.note: read not as a battlefield but as the Latin phrase an old Roman would use for a ground, or justification, for going to war

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a cause or pretext for war, literally an occasion of war.

clue.text: Ready to be seen in popular resort

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a resort is a place one goes to

explanation.surface: A fashionable holiday spot ready for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set up and in position is prepared and ready for use.

clue.text: Heretic can be made to sign confession, for a start

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something new, so they are rearranged
for a start takes the opening letter of the word confession

explanation.surface: An accused heretic might be forced to sign a confession to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges TO SIGN; C, the first letter of 'confession' ('for a start'), ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostics were early Christian sects the Church condemned as holding heretical beliefs about secret knowledge.

clue.text: Record has almost everything wrong

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: all means everything
bum is slang for bad or wrong, as in a bum note

explanation.surface: A recording where nearly everything has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing recording of several tracks.

clue.text: Line a cricket team's following

parts.note: a cricket team is an eleven, written XI, with the possessive S kept on

explanation.surface: A cricket team's batting line-up following on.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive 's gives a real S; 'following' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a straight line about which a body turns or a graph is drawn.

clue.text: Dim student has broken shoulder

indicators.note: the student has broken into the other word, so goes inside it

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A slow student has broken a shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder' is a verb here, to carry; 'Dim' looks like dull-witted but means blurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means blurred or misty, as eyes or light can be.

clue.text: Lake, loch, lough, etc?

parts.note: each listed item is a word meaning a small lake, so the list is a set of synonyms for that old word for a pond, and also just talk

explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake, so lake, loch and lough are words for it; the phrase also means talk with no action.

clue.text: Places of relaxation where some may have dates?

definitions.text: Places of relaxation where some may have dates?

parts.words: Places of relaxation where some may have dates?
parts.note: reads like romantic meeting spots, but the dates are fruit growing on palms in desert watering holes

explanation.definitionFit: Desert springs with palms offer rest to travellers, and date palms grow there.

clue.text: Anyhow, I prefer to make a lot of money

indicators.note: anyhow means in a disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone says that, whatever happens, they would rather get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To profiteer is to make excessive gains, especially by exploiting shortages.

clue.text: What happens as a result of bug in reloading of computer programs?

definitions.text: What happens as a result of bug
definitions.meaning: a bug is a germ, so a sniffly illness begins
restarting a machine from power off

explanation.surface: A virus causes trouble when a computer reloads its programs.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill coming on starts with a germ; in computing a reboot from scratch has the same name.

clue.text: Crest king used in London area

indicators.note: the king is used inside the area, so goes within it

parts.note: Bow is a district in east London
R is rex, king

explanation.surface: A royal crest used in part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow of a hill is its top or crest.

clue.text: Field in which one has to deal with a matter someone's raised

definitions.text: in which one has to deal with a matter someone's raised
definitions.meaning: dealing with, or covering, a point that has been raised

explanation.surface: A field of work where one handles issues others bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a fielding position on the off side; to cover a point is to handle an issue raised.

clue.text: Allow French military leader to circumscribe Council of Europe

indicators.note: to circumscribe is to draw a line around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the Prince de Conde was a great 17th-century French general
CE abbreviates Council of Europe

explanation.surface: A French general is allowed to surround a European body.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to grant or admit something, giving way on it.

clue.text: Infectious sort of chat featured in some TV programmes?

indicators.note: featured in places the anagram inside the other piece

parts.note: cable is a kind of television service

indicators.note: sort of signals a version of the word chat, rearranged

explanation.surface: A contagious kind of chatter on certain television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infectious' sits at the front as the definition; 'sort of' makes ATCH from the chat, and 'featured in' sets it after the first letter of the TV word.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease that is infectious can be picked up from someone else.

clue.text: Impose heavy tax on clothing

definitions.meaning: to hit hard, as a government hitting earners with taxes
British slang for clothes and gear

explanation.surface: A government taxes clothes heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to hit hard, as with taxes, and, in British slang, one's clothes or kit.

clue.text: Engaged revolutionary element in plot

indicators.note: in puts the revolutionary and element inside the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
a Trot is a Trotskyist
He is the symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is involved in a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people engaged to marry are promised to each other.

clue.text: Structure used in French very bad, on reflection

indicators.note: used in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: tres is French for very

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word for bad is read backwards

parts.note: ill means bad

explanation.surface: A building used in France is, thinking it over, very poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' belongs to the first piece, not the definition, and 'Structure' is the definition, not part of the picture; 'on reflection' turns the word for bad backwards, and 'used in' puts that inside the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework for climbing plants.

clue.text: Academic pupil

explanation.surface: A pupil who is academic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a learned expert and, more old-fashioned, a schoolchild.

clue.text: What you take on doctor's orders, maybe?

definitions.text: What you take on doctor's orders, maybe?

parts.words: What you take on doctor's orders, maybe?
parts.note: suggests medicine, but a doctor with a stethoscope tells you to inhale deeply

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor examining your chest asks you to draw air in, deeply.

clue.text: Hotel employee giving signal to start dance

indicators.note: to start puts the signal at the head of the dance

parts.note: a bell is a signal
a hop is a dance

explanation.surface: A hotel worker gives the signal for the dance to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop is a hotel porter who carries luggage, chiefly in American use.

clue.text: Order evident in male habitat

indicators.note: the order is evident inside the male, so it goes within

parts.note: he is a male
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Order is plain to see in a man's living space.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's natural home is its habitat, the place it lives.

clue.text: Party man needing a tonic?

definitions.meaning: a sociable person who mingles well at gatherings
tonic water added to a spirit, as in gin and tonic

explanation.surface: A party-goer needing a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A good mingler is a sociable type; a drink such as tonic added to spirits has the same name.

clue.text: Like medicine bottles adduced as evidence in juvenile court?

definitions.meaning: medicine bottles have caps youngsters cannot open

definitions.text: adduced as evidence in juvenile court?
definitions.meaning: evidence about a youngster, as offered in a youth court

explanation.surface: Medicine bottles offered as evidence in a youth court.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety caps keep youngsters out; read as two words it is evidence about a youngster.

clue.text: Monarch flanked by cook and chauffeur

indicators.note: the monarch has the cook's letters on each side

parts.note: to fry is to cook
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch with a cook on one side and a chauffeur on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferry someone is to drive or carry them about, as a chauffeur does.

clue.text: Organ specialist takes taxi up to hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
H is hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A specialist takes a taxi to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CAB to BAC; 'Organ specialist' suggests a surgeon but is the composer who wrote for the church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: J S Bach was a great organist and composer for the organ.

clue.text: Itinerant trader to fight repeal of act (note 6)

parts.note: to box is to fight

indicators.note: repeal read as re-peal, peeling back, so the law is reversed

parts.note: a law is an act of parliament
lah is the sixth note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A travelling trader fights to have a law repealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeal of' turns LAW to WAL. A boxwallah is an Anglo-Indian word for a pedlar.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a boxwallah was a pedlar going door to door with goods.

clue.text: Divine flower produced by organic horticulture

indicators.note: the letters are produced by the run of these words, sitting across them

explanation.surface: A heavenly flower grown by organic gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: the fluid that ran in the veins of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the ethereal fluid that flowed in the gods' veins instead of blood.

clue.text: Ground Londoners might associate with cricket?

indicators.note: Cockney Londoners drop the initial aitch, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Dickens wrote The Cricket on the Hearth, so the fireside links with crickets

explanation.surface: A soil that Londoners might link with cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the London sport, but is the insect of Dickens's story; Cockneys (working-class East Londoners) say the fireside word without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is soil, the ground under our feet.

clue.text: Express journalist breaking into bank, it's said

indicators.note: breaking into puts the pieces inside the other word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
to put something is to express it
ED is an editor

explanation.surface: An Express journalist reportedly breaks into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the newspaper but is a verb, to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputedly true is so according to report or general belief.
